newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil industry shrugs off planned port strike.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil industry shrugs off planned port strike.

text.p: The Japanese oil industry is unlikely to be affected significantly by a 24-hour nationwide strike planned by two Japanese port workers' unions for March 12, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"I believe the workers belonging (to the two unions) do not handle work related to oil tankers," one official with a leading oil company said.
"I can't immediately see any impact from the strike," a second oil industry source said.
An official with the National Council of Dock Workers' Unions, one of the two unions planning the strike, said its members do not handle work related to the oil industry.
The second union, the Japan Confederation of Port and Transport Workers' Unions, could not immediately be reached for comment.
Other oil industry officials and traders reacted calmly to the news as few anticipated any significant impact from the planned action.

The two unions said they would strike from 8 a.m. on March 12 to protest against a U.S. decision to impose sanctions on Japanese ships calling at U.S. ports, as well as to seek better working conditions.

The U.S. Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) said last week it would impose a $100,000 surcharge on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports from April 14 in retaliation for what it termed "unfavourable restrictive practices" at Japanese ports.
The Japanese port workers' unions are also calling for shorter working hours and job security.
The strike would affect operations at all major ports in Japan, including Yokohama and Kobe.
The two unions also said they would refuse to do any handling work on Sundays starting from March 16.
